verdict: Amazon's sales rose 14% to $213.4B and AWS growth accelerated to 24% — while $2.4B of one-off charges in its stores business held operating income to $25.0B.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and advertising in the US, Canada and Mexico; earned $11.5B of operating income.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Stores and subscriptions outside North America (+11% before currency effects); earned $1.0B of operating income.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Amazon Web Services cloud computing — its fastest growth in 13 quarters; earned $12.5B of operating income, half of Amazon's total.

opex.name: Fulfillment
opex.note: Warehouses and delivery — getting orders to doors.

opex.name: Technology & infrastructure
opex.note: Engineers and the tech behind the store and AWS; up 25% YoY with the AI build-out.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Amazon's own services and sales teams.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office costs: finance, legal and admin.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Mostly this quarter's special charges: Italy tax-dispute resolutions and a lawsuit settlement, severance, and store asset impairments.

otherDetail: Total non-operating income of $1,628M: $1,130M of interest income and $1,177M of other income, less $679M of interest expense. Equity-method activity took off another $467M after tax.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: AWS growth is accelerating again
takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 24% to $35.6B — the fastest in 13 quarters — and produced $12.5B of operating income: half of Amazon's total profit from 17% of its sales. Amazon's own chips business (Trainium and Graviton) passed a $10B annual run rate, growing at triple-digit rates.

takeaways.title: One-off charges in the stores business
takeaways.text: Operating income includes $1.1B for resolving tax disputes tied to the stores business in Italy and settling a lawsuit, $730M of severance costs, and $610M of asset impairments, mainly on physical stores. Without them, operating income would have been $27.4B.

takeaways.title: The AI build-out swallows the cash
takeaways.text: Full-year free cash flow fell to $11.2B because spending on property and equipment jumped $50.7B year over year — mostly AI. Amazon expects to invest about $200B in capex across 2026.

oneTimers: Operating income includes three special charges totaling about $2.4B: $1.1B for the resolution of tax disputes associated with Amazon's stores business in Italy and the settlement of a lawsuit, $730M in estimated severance costs, and $610M in asset impairments primarily related to physical stores. Excluding these charges, operating income would have been $27.4B.
